Correspondence with the supplied proof:
- coordinate_functional = step 1: Λ_i := L(·•e_i) is linear and has the same local bounds.
- jordan_decomposition = step 1(B) and steps 2–3. The variation V is additive (by clamping) and ℝ≥0-homogeneous; V̂ := toRealPositiveLinear V; P := V̂ + Λ ≥ 0; Λ = P − V̂.
- common_density = steps 4, 5, 6 and 8 for a finite family. RMK measures a_i, b_i are dominated by μ₀ = Σ(a_i + b_i); Lebesgue decomposition gives densities; integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul gives P_i f − N_i f = ∫ f ρ_i dμ₀.
- coordinate_assembly = steps 7 and 9: ν := Σ ρ_i e_i, g = Σ g_i e_i, and L g = Σ ∫ g_i ρ_i dμ₀ = ∫ ⟨g, ν⟩ dμ₀.
The children are mutually independent (depends_on = []), and dependencies are acyclic.

How the children imply the selected statement:
(1) For each i, coordinate_functional gives a linear Λ_i with L g = Λ_i f whenever g(x) = f(x)•e_i, and Λ_i is locally bounded.
(2) For each i, jordan_decomposition gives positive functionals P_i and N_i with Λ_i f = P_i f − N_i f.
(3) common_density with m = d, Λ₁ = P and Λ₂ = N gives μ₀, finite on compacts, and measurable ρ_i, integrable on compacts, with P_i f − N_i f = ∫ f ρ_i dμ₀.
(4) Hence the hypothesis of coordinate_assembly holds: if g(x) = f(x)•e_i for all x, then L g = Λ_i f = P_i f − N_i f = ∫ f(x) ρ_i(x) dμ₀.
(5) coordinate_assembly then gives a measurable ν, integrable on compacts, with L g = ∫ ⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩ dμ₀ for all g. Together with IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ₀ from (3), this is exactly the selected conclusion.

subproblems.title: Coordinate functionals of a locally bounded functional on C_c(X, ℝ^d)
subproblems.statement: Let X be a topological space and d ∈ ℕ. Let H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (ℝ^d with the Euclidean norm) and, for i ∈ Fin d, let e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 be the i-th standard unit vector. Let L : C_c(X, H) → ℝ be real linear and locally bounded: for every compact K ⊆ X there is M ∈ ℝ with |L g| ≤ M for all g ∈ C_c(X, H) with tsupport g ⊆ K and ‖g(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x. Then for every i ∈ Fin d there is a real linear map Λ : C_c(X, ℝ) → ℝ with two properties. (i) L g = Λ f whenever f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ), g ∈ C_c(X, H) and g(x) = f(x)·e_i for all x ∈ X. (ii) Λ is locally bounded: for every compact K ⊆ X there is M ∈ ℝ with |Λ f| ≤ M for all f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) with tsupport f ⊆ K and |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (d : ℕ) (L : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ), (∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), tsupport g ⊆ K → (∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ 1) → |L g| ≤ M) → ∀ i : Fin d, ∃ Λ : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ, (∀ (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ) (g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))), (∀ x, g x = f x • EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) → L g = Λ f) ∧ ∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ, tsupport f ⊆ K → (∀ x, |f x| ≤ 1) → |Λ f| ≤ M
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the selected node's supplied proof (the scalar functionals Λ_i(f) := L(f•e_i)). Claim (B), the rescaled bound, is not needed for this statement; it is proved in the jordan_decomposition sibling.
Notation: H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); e := e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, so ‖e‖ = 1 (PiLp.norm_single).
1. Fix i ∈ Fin d. The map c : ℝ → H, c(t) := t•e, is continuous (product of the identity and a constant) and c(0) = 0.
2. For f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) put T f := f.compLeft c ∈ C_c(X, H). Since c(0) = 0, (T f)(x) = c(f(x)) = f(x)•e for every x ∈ X (CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.compLeft_apply). Mathematically, c∘f is continuous and vanishes wherever f does, so its closed support lies in the compact set tsupport f.
3. T is ℝ-linear. For all x, (T(f₁+f₂))(x) = (f₁(x)+f₂(x))•e = (T f₁)(x) + (T f₂)(x), and (T(r•f))(x) = (r·f(x))•e = r•((T f)(x)). Elements of C_c(X, H) with the same values are equal (extensionality).
4. Define Λ := L ∘ T, an ℝ-linear map C_c(X, ℝ) → ℝ.
5. (Representation clause.) Let f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) and g ∈ C_c(X, H) with g(x) = f(x)•e for all x. By step 2, g(x) = (T f)(x) for all x, so g = T f by extensionality, and L g = L(T f) = Λ f.
6. (Bound clause.) Let K ⊆ X be compact and let M be the constant from the hypothesis on L for this K. Let f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) with tsupport f ⊆ K and |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, and put g := T f.
 (a) Since g(x) = f(x)•e, g(x) = 0 wherever f(x) = 0. So support g ⊆ support f, and taking closures, tsupport g ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ K (Lean: tsupport_smul_subset_left).
 (b) For every x, ‖g(x)‖ = |f(x)|·‖e‖ = |f(x)| ≤ 1.
 By the hypothesis on L, |Λ f| = |L g| ≤ M. M depends only on K, so it is the required constant.
7. Steps 4–6 give, for each i ∈ Fin d, a linear map Λ with properties (i) and (ii).
proof_key_steps: The map t ↦ t•e_i is continuous and vanishes at 0, so T f := f.compLeft (t ↦ t•e_i) lies in C_c(X, H) and (T f)(x) = f(x)•e_i.
T is ℝ-linear (check values pointwise, then extensionality); set Λ := L ∘ T.
If g(x) = f(x)•e_i for all x, then g = T f by extensionality, so L g = Λ f.
tsupport(T f) ⊆ tsupport f and ‖(T f)(x)‖ = |f(x)|, so L's bound at K gives |Λ f| ≤ M with the same constant.

subproblems.title: Jordan decomposition of a locally bounded functional on C_c(X, ℝ)
subproblems.statement: Let X be a topological space and let Λ : C_c(X, ℝ) → ℝ be a real linear map that is locally bounded: for every compact K ⊆ X there is M ∈ ℝ with |Λ f| ≤ M for all f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) with tsupport f ⊆ K and |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Then there are positive linear functionals Λ₁, Λ₂ on C_c(X, ℝ), that is, elements of C_c(X, ℝ) →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ (ℝ-linear and order-preserving), such that Λ f = Λ₁ f − Λ₂ f for every f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (Λ : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ), (∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ, tsupport f ⊆ K → (∀ x, |f x| ≤ 1) → |Λ f| ≤ M) → ∃ Λ₁ Λ₂ : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ, ∀ f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ, Λ f = Λ₁ f - Λ₂ f
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 Claim (B), step 2 and step 3 of the selected node's supplied proof, specialized to one scalar functional Λ (the proof's Λ_i).
Notation: for f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ≥0), f̃ := f.toReal ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) with f̃(x) = f(x) (CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.toReal).
1. (Scaled bound.) Let K ⊆ X be compact and M_K its constant from the hypothesis.
 Claim: if f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ), tsupport f ⊆ K, s ∈ ℝ, s ≥ 0 and |f(x)| ≤ s for all x, then |Λ f| ≤ s·M_K.
 Case s = 0: |f(x)| ≤ 0 gives f(x) = 0 for all x, so f = 0 and |Λ f| = 0 = s·M_K.
 Case s > 0: s⁻¹f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) has tsupport(s⁻¹f) ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ K and |s⁻¹f(x)| = s⁻¹|f(x)| ≤ 1. By hypothesis s⁻¹|Λ f| = |Λ(s⁻¹f)| ≤ M_K, i.e. |Λ f| ≤ s·M_K.
2. (The sets A_f.) For f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ≥0) let A_f := {h ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) : |h(x)| ≤ f(x) for all x}.
 (a) 0 ∈ A_f.
 (b) If h ∈ A_f and f(x) = 0, then |h(x)| ≤ 0, so h(x) = 0. Hence support h ⊆ support f and, taking closures, tsupport h ⊆ tsupport f. tsupport f is compact because f has compact support.
 (c) f̃ is continuous with compact support, hence bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support): there is C with f(x) ≤ |f̃(x)| ≤ C for all x. Put s_f := max(C, 0) ≥ 0.
 (d) For h ∈ A_f: tsupport h ⊆ tsupport f and |h(x)| ≤ f(x) ≤ s_f. Step 1 with K := tsupport f gives Λ h ≤ |Λ h| ≤ s_f·M_{tsupport f}.
 So Λ(A_f) := {Λ h : h ∈ A_f} contains Λ 0 = 0 and is bounded above.
3. (Variation.) Define V(f) := sup Λ(A_f) ∈ ℝ. By step 2, Λ h ≤ V(f) for every h ∈ A_f, and V(f) ≥ Λ 0 = 0.
4. (V dominates |Λ| on the positive cone.) For f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ≥0), both f̃ and −f̃ lie in A_f, since |±f̃(x)| = f(x). Hence Λ f̃ ≤ V(f) and −Λ f̃ = Λ(−f̃) ≤ V(f), i.e. |Λ f̃| ≤ V(f).
5. (Additivity: V(f₁+f₂) = V(f₁) + V(f₂) for f₁, f₂ ∈ C_c(X, ℝ≥0).)
 (≥) If h₁ ∈ A_{f₁} and h₂ ∈ A_{f₂}, then |h₁(x)+h₂(x)| ≤ |h₁(x)| + |h₂(x)| ≤ f₁(x) + f₂(x). So h₁+h₂ ∈ A_{f₁+f₂} and Λ h₁ + Λ h₂ = Λ(h₁+h₂) ≤ V(f₁+f₂).
 Fix h₁. Then Λ h₂ ≤ V(f₁+f₂) − Λ h₁ for all h₂ ∈ A_{f₂}. Since A_{f₂} ≠ ∅, the least-upper-bound property gives V(f₂) ≤ V(f₁+f₂) − Λ h₁.
 Hence Λ h₁ ≤ V(f₁+f₂) − V(f₂) for all h₁ ∈ A_{f₁}, so V(f₁) ≤ V(f₁+f₂) − V(f₂).
 (≤) Let h ∈ A_{f₁+f₂}. Put h₁ := (h ⊓ f̃₁) ⊔ (−f̃₁) ∈ C_c(X, ℝ), so h₁(x) = max(min(h(x), f₁(x)), −f₁(x)). C_c(X, ℝ) is a lattice under pointwise max/min (CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.sup_apply, inf_apply). Put h₂ := h − h₁ ∈ C_c(X, ℝ).
 Fix x and write a := h(x), p := f₁(x) ≥ 0, q := f₂(x) ≥ 0, so |a| ≤ p+q.
 Since −p ≤ p, h₁(x) = max(min(a, p), −p) ∈ [−p, p]. So |h₁(x)| ≤ p, and h₁ ∈ A_{f₁}.
 Now h₂(x) = a − h₁(x):
 - if −p ≤ a ≤ p, then h₁(x) = a and h₂(x) = 0;
 - if a > p, then h₁(x) = p and 0 < h₂(x) = a − p ≤ q;
 - if a < −p, then h₁(x) = −p and −q ≤ h₂(x) = a + p < 0.
 In every case |h₂(x)| ≤ q, so h₂ ∈ A_{f₂}.
 Therefore Λ h = Λ h₁ + Λ h₂ ≤ V(f₁) + V(f₂). Taking the supremum over h ∈ A_{f₁+f₂} gives V(f₁+f₂) ≤ V(f₁) + V(f₂).
6. (Homogeneity: V(t•f) = t·V(f) for t ∈ ℝ≥0.)
 Case t = 0: t•f = 0 and A_0 = {0}, because |h(x)| ≤ 0 forces h = 0. So V(0) = sup{0} = 0 = 0·V(f).
 Case t > 0:
 - If h ∈ A_{t f}, then t⁻¹h ∈ A_f because |t⁻¹h(x)| ≤ t⁻¹·t·f(x) = f(x). So Λ h = t·Λ(t⁻¹h) ≤ t·V(f), giving V(t f) ≤ t·V(f).
 - If h ∈ A_f, then t h ∈ A_{t f}, so Λ h = t⁻¹·Λ(t h) ≤ t⁻¹·V(t f). So V(f) ≤ t⁻¹·V(t f), i.e. t·V(f) ≤ V(t f).
7. (A positive functional V̂.) By steps 3, 5 and 6, f ↦ V(f), viewed in ℝ≥0 since V(f) ≥ 0, is an ℝ≥0-linear map V : C_c(X, ℝ≥0) →ₗ[ℝ≥0] ℝ≥0. Let V̂ := CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.toRealPositiveLinear V. This is a positive ℝ-linear functional on C_c(X, ℝ) with V̂(f̃) = V(f) for all f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ≥0) (eq_toRealPositiveLinear_toReal).
8. (Jordan decomposition.) Let P := V̂ + Λ, an ℝ-linear map C_c(X, ℝ) → ℝ.
 P is positive. Let k ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) with k ≥ 0 and put k⁺ := nnrealPart k ∈ C_c(X, ℝ≥0). Then k⁺(x) = max(k(x), 0) = k(x), so k = (k⁺)~ and V̂ k = V(k⁺). Step 4 with f = k⁺ gives |Λ k| ≤ V(k⁺). Hence P k = V(k⁺) + Λ k ≥ |Λ k| + Λ k ≥ 0.
 So Λ₁ := P, packaged as a positive linear map by PositiveLinearMap.mk₀ (nonnegativity on the cone suffices by linearity), and Λ₂ := V̂ are positive linear functionals on C_c(X, ℝ). For every f, Λ₁ f − Λ₂ f = (V̂ f + Λ f) − V̂ f = Λ f.
proof_key_steps: Scaled bound: if tsupport f ⊆ K and |f| ≤ s with s ≥ 0, then |Λ f| ≤ s·M_K (case s = 0, else rescale by s⁻¹).
For f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ≥0), A_f = {h : |h| ≤ f} contains 0, and its members have tsupport ⊆ tsupport f and are bounded by s_f; so Λ(A_f) is bounded above and V(f) := sup Λ(A_f) ≥ 0.
±f̃ ∈ A_f, so |Λ f̃| ≤ V(f).
V is additive: ≥ via h₁+h₂ ∈ A_{f₁+f₂} and two suprema; ≤ via the clamp h₁ = max(min(h, f₁), −f₁) and the three-case bound |h − h₁| ≤ f₂.
V is ℝ≥0-homogeneous (t = 0: A_0 = {0}; t > 0: h ↦ t h maps A_f onto A_{tf}), so V is ℝ≥0-linear; V̂ := toRealPositiveLinear V.
P := V̂ + Λ is positive since V̂ k = V(nnrealPart k) ≥ |Λ k| for k ≥ 0; Λ = P − V̂.

subproblems.title: Common dominating measure and densities for finitely many RMK measures
subproblems.statement: Let X be a locally compact Hausdorff space with a countable basis, equipped with its Borel σ-algebra. Let m ∈ ℕ and, for i ∈ Fin m, let Λ₁ᵢ and Λ₂ᵢ be positive linear functionals on C_c(X, ℝ), i.e. elements of C_c(X, ℝ) →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ. Then there are a measure μ₀ on X that is finite on compact sets and measurable functions ρᵢ : X → ℝ (i ∈ Fin m), each μ₀-integrable on every compact subset of X, such that Λ₁ᵢ f − Λ₂ᵢ f = ∫ f(x)·ρᵢ(x) dμ₀(x) for every i ∈ Fin m and every f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [SecondCountableTopology X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (m : ℕ) (Λ₁ Λ₂ : Fin m → (CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ)), ∃ (μ₀ : Measure X) (ρ : Fin m → X → ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ₀ ∧ (∀ i, Measurable (ρ i)) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → IntegrableOn (ρ i) K μ₀) ∧ ∀ (i : Fin m) (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ), Λ₁ i f - Λ₂ i f = ∫ x, f x * ρ i x ∂μ₀
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4, 5, 6 and 8 of the selected node's supplied proof, stated for an arbitrary finite family. The selected proof applies it with m = d, Λ₁ᵢ = P_i and Λ₂ᵢ = V̂_i.
1. (Riesz–Markov–Kakutani.) For i ∈ Fin m let bᵢ := RealRMK.rieszMeasure Λ₁ᵢ and aᵢ := RealRMK.rieszMeasure Λ₂ᵢ. These are measures on the Borel σ-algebra of X. They are regular (RealRMK.regular_rieszMeasure), hence finite on compact sets (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts). For every f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ), ∫ f dbᵢ = Λ₁ᵢ f and ∫ f daᵢ = Λ₂ᵢ f (RealRMK.integral_rieszMeasure).
2. (Dominating measure.) Let μ₀ := Σ_{i ∈ Fin m} (aᵢ + bᵢ). For compact K, μ₀(K) = Σ_i (aᵢ(K) + bᵢ(K)) is a finite sum of finite terms, so μ₀(K) < ∞. Thus μ₀ is finite on compact sets. (For m = 0, μ₀ = 0.)
3. (σ-finiteness.) X is locally compact with a countable basis, hence σ-compact (sigmaCompactSpace_of_locallyCompact_secondCountable). A measure finite on compact sets of a σ-compact space is σ-finite (SigmaFinite.of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts). So μ₀ and all aᵢ, bᵢ are σ-finite, and each pair (ξ, μ₀) with ξ ∈ {aᵢ, bᵢ} has a Lebesgue decomposition.
4. (Absolute continuity.) Let s ⊆ X with μ₀(s) = 0. Then Σ_j (aⱼ(s) + bⱼ(s)) = 0 is a finite sum of elements of [0, ∞], so every term is 0; in particular aᵢ(s) = 0 and bᵢ(s) = 0. Hence aᵢ ≪ μ₀ and bᵢ ≪ μ₀.
5. (Density representation.) Let ξ be one of aᵢ, bᵢ, and let δ := ξ.rnDeriv μ₀ : X → [0, ∞], which is measurable (Measure.measurable_rnDeriv). The Lebesgue decomposition gives ξ = ξ.singularPart μ₀ + μ₀.withDensity δ (Measure.haveLebesgueDecomposition_add). Since ξ ≪ μ₀, ξ.singularPart μ₀ = 0 (Measure.singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac), so ξ = μ₀.withDensity δ. Moreover δ(x) < ∞ for μ₀-a.e. x (Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top, since ξ is σ-finite).
6. (Local integrability of the densities.) Let K be compact. Since ξ(K) < ∞, ∫⁻_K δ dμ₀ < ∞ (Measure.lintegral_rnDeriv_lt_top_of_measure_ne_top). As δ is measurable, x ↦ (δ x).toReal is integrable for μ₀ restricted to K (integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top), i.e. μ₀-integrable on K.
7. (Integrals against ξ.) Let f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ).
 (a) Since ξ = μ₀.withDensity δ with δ measurable and finite μ₀-a.e., ∫ f dξ = ∫ (δ x).toReal·f(x) dμ₀(x) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul).
 (b) x ↦ (δ x).toReal·f(x) is μ₀-integrable. K_f := tsupport f is compact. f is continuous, hence Borel measurable, and bounded: |f(x)| ≤ C for all x, being continuous with compact support. By step 6, (δ ·).toReal is integrable on K_f, so the product is integrable on K_f (integrable times bounded measurable, Integrable.mul_bdd). It vanishes outside K_f, where f = 0, so it is integrable on X (IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero).
8. (Definition of ρ.) Put αᵢ := aᵢ.rnDeriv μ₀, βᵢ := bᵢ.rnDeriv μ₀ and ρᵢ(x) := (βᵢ x).toReal − (αᵢ x).toReal. Each ρᵢ is measurable: toReal of a measurable [0, ∞]-valued function is measurable, and so is a difference of measurable functions. For compact K, ρᵢ is μ₀-integrable on K, as the difference of the two integrable functions given by step 6 for ξ = bᵢ and ξ = aᵢ.
9. (Representation.) For i ∈ Fin m and f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ):
 Λ₁ᵢ f − Λ₂ᵢ f = ∫ f dbᵢ − ∫ f daᵢ (step 1)
 = ∫ (βᵢ x).toReal·f(x) dμ₀ − ∫ (αᵢ x).toReal·f(x) dμ₀ (step 7(a))
 = ∫ ((βᵢ x).toReal − (αᵢ x).toReal)·f(x) dμ₀ (linearity of the integral; both integrands are integrable by step 7(b))
 = ∫ f(x)·ρᵢ(x) dμ₀(x).
10. Steps 2, 8 and 9 show that μ₀ and ρ have all the required properties.
proof_key_steps: RMK: aᵢ := rieszMeasure Λ₂ᵢ and bᵢ := rieszMeasure Λ₁ᵢ are finite on compacts with ∫ f daᵢ = Λ₂ᵢ f and ∫ f dbᵢ = Λ₁ᵢ f.
μ₀ := Σᵢ (aᵢ + bᵢ) is finite on compacts; X is σ-compact, so μ₀, aᵢ, bᵢ are σ-finite; μ₀(s) = 0 forces aᵢ(s) = bᵢ(s) = 0, so aᵢ, bᵢ ≪ μ₀.
Lebesgue decomposition + singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac: ξ = μ₀.withDensity (ξ.rnDeriv μ₀), with a measurable, a.e.-finite density whose lintegral over each compact set is finite.
ρᵢ := (βᵢ).toReal − (αᵢ).toReal is measurable and integrable on compacts.
integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul plus integrability of density × f (bounded, compact support) gives Λ₁ᵢ f − Λ₂ᵢ f = ∫ f ρᵢ dμ₀.

subproblems.title: Assembling coordinate density representations into a vector representation
subproblems.statement: Let X be a topological space with a σ-algebra containing all open sets, d ∈ ℕ, H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) and e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for i ∈ Fin d. Let L : C_c(X, H) → ℝ be real linear, μ₀ a measure on X, and ρᵢ : X → ℝ (i ∈ Fin d) measurable functions, each μ₀-integrable on every compact subset of X. Assume L g = ∫ f(x)·ρᵢ(x) dμ₀(x) whenever i ∈ Fin d, f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ), g ∈ C_c(X, H) and g(x) = f(x)·e_i for all x ∈ X. Then there is a measurable ν : X → H, μ₀-integrable on every compact subset of X, such that L g = ∫ ⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩ dμ₀(x) for every g ∈ C_c(X, H).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [OpensMeasurableSpace X] (d : ℕ) (L : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (μ₀ : Measure X) (ρ : Fin d → X → ℝ), (∀ i, Measurable (ρ i)) → (∀ i, ∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → IntegrableOn (ρ i) K μ₀) → (∀ (i : Fin d) (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ) (g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))), (∀ x, g x = f x • EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) → L g = ∫ x, f x * ρ i x ∂μ₀) → ∃ ν : X → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), Measurable ν ∧ (∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → IntegrableOn ν K μ₀) ∧ ∀ g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), L g = ∫ x, inner ℝ (g x) (ν x) ∂μ₀
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 7 and 9 of the selected node's supplied proof.
Notation: for v ∈ H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), v_j is its j-th coordinate. So (e_i)_j = 1 if j = i and 0 otherwise, and ⟨v, w⟩ = Σ_j v_j·w_j (PiLp.inner_apply; the real inner product on ℝ is multiplication).
1. (Definition of ν.) ν(x) := Σ_{i ∈ Fin d} ρᵢ(x)·e_i. Then ν(x)_j = Σ_i ρᵢ(x)·(e_i)_j = ρⱼ(x) for every j.
2. (Measurability.) Each x ↦ ρᵢ(x)·e_i is measurable: a measurable real function times a fixed vector (Measurable.smul_const). A finite sum of measurable H-valued functions is measurable (Finset.measurable_sum). So ν is measurable.
3. (Integrability on compact sets.) Let K be compact. Each x ↦ ρᵢ(x)·e_i is μ₀-integrable on K, since ρᵢ is (Integrable.smul_const). Hence the finite sum ν is μ₀-integrable on K (integrable_finsetSum).
4. (Coordinates of g.) Fix g ∈ C_c(X, H).
 The coordinate map pᵢ : H → ℝ, v ↦ v_i, is continuous linear with pᵢ(0) = 0. So gᵢ := g.compLeft pᵢ ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) and gᵢ(x) = g(x)_i.
 The map cᵢ : ℝ → H, t ↦ t·e_i, is continuous with cᵢ(0) = 0. So Gᵢ := gᵢ.compLeft cᵢ ∈ C_c(X, H) and Gᵢ(x) = gᵢ(x)·e_i (CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.compLeft_apply).
5. (Decomposition of g.) g = Σ_i Gᵢ in C_c(X, H): for every x and j, (Σ_i Gᵢ(x))_j = Σ_i g(x)_i·(e_i)_j = g(x)_j. Elements of C_c(X, H) with the same values are equal; the value of a finite sum is the pointwise sum (CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.coe_sum).
6. (Applying the hypothesis.) By linearity of L and the hypothesis with f := gᵢ and g := Gᵢ (valid since Gᵢ(x) = gᵢ(x)·e_i for all x):
 L g = Σ_i L Gᵢ = Σ_i ∫ gᵢ(x)·ρᵢ(x) dμ₀(x).
7. (Integrability of gᵢρᵢ.) K := tsupport gᵢ is compact. gᵢ is continuous, hence measurable since open sets are measurable, and bounded: |gᵢ(x)| ≤ C for some C, being continuous with compact support. ρᵢ is μ₀-integrable on K, so x ↦ gᵢ(x)·ρᵢ(x) is μ₀-integrable on K (bounded measurable times integrable, Integrable.bdd_mul). It vanishes outside K, where gᵢ = 0, so it is μ₀-integrable on X (IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero).
8. (Interchanging sum and integral.) By step 7, Σ_i ∫ gᵢρᵢ dμ₀ = ∫ Σ_i gᵢ(x)·ρᵢ(x) dμ₀(x) (integral_finsetSum).
9. (Inner product.) For every x, Σ_i gᵢ(x)·ρᵢ(x) = Σ_i g(x)_i·ν(x)_i = ⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩, by steps 1 and 4.
10. Combining steps 6, 8 and 9 gives L g = ∫ ⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩ dμ₀(x) for every g ∈ C_c(X, H). Together with steps 2 and 3, ν has all the required properties.
proof_key_steps: Define ν := Σᵢ ρᵢ e_i; then ν(x)_j = ρⱼ(x), and ν is measurable and integrable on compacts as a finite sum of ρᵢ·(constant vector).
For g ∈ C_c(X,H), the coordinates gᵢ = pᵢ ∘ g and Gᵢ = gᵢ(·)e_i lie in C_c, and g = Σᵢ Gᵢ (coordinatewise extensionality).
Linearity plus the hypothesis give L g = Σᵢ ∫ gᵢ ρᵢ dμ₀.
Each gᵢρᵢ is integrable: bounded continuous times integrable on the compact tsupport, and zero outside it.
Swap the finite sum and the integral, then use ⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩ = Σᵢ g(x)ᵢ ρᵢ(x).
